evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.field: 形義通解；甲骨文、金文用例
evidence.text: The database analyzes the oracle-bone and bronze forms as 目 plus 卩, with 卩 representing a kneeling person and the eye emphasized to express seeing. It distinguishes 見 from 視 by the seated versus standing human figure, with a noted exception. Oracle-bone uses include seeing and audience; it also reports a reading as 獻 ‘offer sacrificial goods’. Bronze examples include seeing, audience, and a passive auxiliary use. These are source-reported interpretations and examples; no specific earliest dated inscription was verified here.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 見

evidence.source: 中央研究院漢字構形資料庫
evidence.field: 字形演變；甲骨文、金文、楚系簡帛、小篆
evidence.text: The database indexes oracle-bone forms (collection 6790), bronze forms (集成02612), Chu bamboo and silk forms, and seal script. Its explanation says the graph places a human form under a prominent eye and means seeing with the eyes. This supports a graphic history from ancient person-and-eye forms to the regular form, but the accessed page provides no dated specimen sequence or detailed account of intermediate graphic changes.
evidence.title: 漢字「見」：字形演變

evidence.source: Shuowen.org, quoting 說文解字 and 段玉裁注
evidence.text: The Eastern Han dictionary entry defines 見 as ‘視也’ and analyzes it as 从儿从目. Duan Yucai explains this as ‘用目之人也’ (‘a person using the eyes’) and calls it a huiyi analysis. The Shuowen account concerns the received seal/regular graph analysis; it should not be treated as independent proof of every detail of the earlier oracle-bone form.
evidence.kind: historical dictionary text and later annotation
evidence.title: 說文解字「見」

evidence.source: Varying source analyses: CUHK database and 說文解字 / Duan Yucai
evidence.text: The CUHK paleographic database identifies the person component in oracle-bone and bronze forms as 卩 (kneeling person); Shuowen parses the later graph as 儿 plus 目, and Duan glosses it as a person using the eyes. The dossier's claims that the ancient lower element is 卩 and the Shuowen element is 儿 therefore belong to different source analyses/script stages. Neither supports treating the lower element as a phonetic component. No evidence here establishes corruption of the graph.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 見

evidence.source: Baxter–Sagart dataset, local row checked; Unicode Unihan lookup interface (individual lookup unavailable)
evidence.text: The local Baxter–Sagart rows give 見 jiàn ‘see’: Middle Chinese kenH, Old Chinese *[k]ˤen-s; 見 xiàn ‘appear’: henH, *N-[k]ˤen-s; and xiàn ‘cause to appear, introduce’: henH, *m-[k]ˤen-s. The two xiàn entries are distinct reconstructed readings/derivations, not extra transcriptions of jiàn. This character has no sound component at issue, so no component-to-host sound comparison is claimed. Exact local Unihan_Readings rows for 見 and 见 were absent, and the tracked HSK extract did not cover either. The specified official per-character Unihan pages were attempted but returned internal errors; no kMandarin value is asserted from them.
evidence.kind: local structured dataset cross-check plus failed official lookup
evidence.title: Unihan Database Lookup: U+898B (lookup attempt failed)

evidence.source: 中华人民共和国国务院 / 中国文字改革委员会, 简化字总表 (1986 republication, transcribed by Wikisource)
evidence.text: The table maps 見 to 见. This confirms the standardized simplified/traditional correspondence but does not itself identify the historical cursive exemplar or establish the date at which the simplified shape first appeared.
evidence.kind: officially issued standard reproduced in a public text edition
evidence.title: 简化字总表（1986年版）

evidence.text: Unicode explains that its lookup interface provides access to Unihan properties for individual ideographs and that Unihan.zip contains the latest data files. The interface page was inspected, but direct lookup pages for 見 and 见 failed in this session; this documentation is not evidence for either character's specific reading.
evidence.title: Unihan Database Lookup

evidence.text: UAX #38 documents the Unihan database and its property set, including kMandarin. This establishes the scope of the metadata field, not an ancient sound relationship or the values for the two individual characters.
evidence.title: UAX #38: Unicode Han Database (Unihan)

gaps: No exact specimen-level earliest attestation, inscription identifier/date, or chronology of the cited oracle-bone and bronze uses was verified. Treat Late Shang dating as an expected contextual range only if separately sourced; this research did not establish it for the specific specimens.

The reported oracle-bone use read as 獻 is a whole-graph borrowing/phonetic-loan claim, distinct from the graphic composition of 見. The inspected source asserts the reading and offering sense but the underlying inscription examples and comparative sound evidence were not retrieved; the original name/pronunciation of any depicted object is not implicated or established.

No detailed, sourced sequence for graphic transitions between ancient forms, seal script, clerical/regular forms, and the simplified 见 was established. The corpus index confirms several script categories, and the standard confirms the 見/见 mapping, but neither proves a particular shape's chronology or corruption.

The modern readings jiàn and xiàn are present in the dossier and Baxter–Sagart rows for 見, but exact kMandarin rows for 見 and 见 could not be verified externally. The host/component reading comparison requirement does not apply because no phonetic component is proposed.
There is no support in the inspected evidence for the dossier's Proto-Sino-Tibetan *ken claim. It is not adopted here.

Earliest semantic links and later extensions are not a comprehensive historical semantic chronology: source summaries report seeing, audience, offering, and passive uses but provide no fully dated sequence establishing when or how each extension arose.

No graphic corruption is demonstrated. The claimed草书 derivation of 见 is plausible in the dossier and search results but was not independently evidenced by an inspected historical cursive specimen or a specialist primary analysis.
